factors.name: Tata group leadership transition
factors.status: N Chandrasekaran resigned as Tata Sons chairman on 12 August 2026, staying until 20 February 2027. The cause is an unresolved February 2026 board meeting at which Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata blocked his renewal as director over losses at certain group companies — 'no resolution has been reached till date.' Six Tata names sit in the Nifty 50 carrying 8.95% weight (TCS 4.0, Tata Motors 1.6, Titan 1.3, Tata Steel 1.0, Tata Consumer 0.6, Trent 0.45). TCS fell ~4% on the announcement, Rs 35,000 cr of market value, and contributes -29.0 index points over three sessions.
factors.transmission: A governance discount applied to a fixed 8.95% block of index weight, transmitted through TCS above all (4.0% weight, and the group's largest listed profit pool). Unlike a macro factor this has NO real-economy channel and no second-order path into other sectors — which is why the index fell while India VIX FELL. It is a repricing of specific cash flows' governance risk, not a change in the discount rate. It resolves on named dates, not on data.

factors.name: AI capex ROI
factors.status: Token prices have fallen ~10x a year (≈$60/M in 2021 to ≈$0.06 by mid-2026) while hyperscaler capex runs $700-900bn for 2026 (+36% YoY, ~75% AI-specific). Sequoia puts the annual revenue gap at ~$600bn; investment is scaling ~50% faster than revenue. The market has already flipped from rewarding capex to punishing it — Meta -9.25% in a session for RAISING guidance. Korea and Taiwan de-rated violently in late July.
factors.transmission: Two opposite legs on different clocks. NEAR TERM the Nifty takes this through global beta only — India has almost no AI-capex exposure in the index, and the AI-infra winners sit outside it. MEDIUM TERM the same absence is the rotation case: EM money crowded into Korea/Taiwan (KOSPI was +41.5% YTD in USD even after a ~40% drawdown) has gains to redeploy, and India is the under-owned alternative after ~-$27bn of 2026 outflows. The one genuine fundamental casualty is Nifty IT (13% weight, already ~39% off its 2024 peak): cheaper tokens validate the services-pricing deflation that is compressing its multiple. The whole rotation leg is gated on the US rate path — a hot CPI firms the dollar and caps EM inflows.

facts.note: TAIEX fell 2,030.83 pts (-4.65%) to 41,603.36, its third steepest session ever; analysts cited fear that cloud providers' AI investments 'will not generate adequate sales'. TSMC -2.98% (~560 index pts); Nanya, Winbond, UMC, MediaTek limit-down at -10%; foreign institutions sold NT$87.56bn in one day. Trigger: Alphabet reporting negative cash flows.

KOSPI erased ~40% from a peak set barely a month earlier — ~$2.18tn over two sessions (-11%, then -6%) — on 'reduced interest in chipmakers', amplified by single-stock leveraged ETFs. Still +41.5% YTD in USD and 2026's best major market.

Capex-to-revenue divergence ~46%, worse than the 32% of the 2001 telecom cycle; capital intensity now 45-57% of revenue. Amazon $200bn, Alphabet $175-185bn, Meta up to $145bn, Microsoft >$120bn for 2026.

Token deflation splits the field: model providers squeezed (OpenAI ~33% gross margin), chipmakers still fat (Nvidia 63% net, TSMC 46.5%, Micron 56%). Chinese open models at ~46% share. Volume is NOT offsetting price — Google went 9.7tn tokens/month (2023) to 3.2 quadrillion (May 2026) and revenue per unit still fell.

MIT: 95% of enterprise GenAI pilots produced zero measurable P&L impact on ~$30-40bn of spend. Credible estimates put meaningful agentic adoption 12-24 months out — that is the gap that has to close before the capex earns anything.

watch: Hyperscaler capex guidance at the next results round — a CUT is the signal, and it lands on Korea/Taiwan chip names before it reaches anything Indian.
Whether foreign selling in Taiwan/Korea shows up as Indian buying within weeks, or just goes to cash — the FII 20-day figure is the tell, not the price.
Nifty IT: token deflation is a structural headwind for services pricing regardless of which way the capex trade breaks.
US CPI — a hot print firms the dollar and shuts the rotation leg before it starts.

factors.name: IT services AI deflation and pricing pressure
factors.status: Clients are shrinking existing contracts to fund AI work rather than adding budget. Google cut ~$50m off a ~$200m annual HCLTech application-development and engineering contract as part of a wider cost programme touching several vendors; Meta trimmed a Wipro deal by $15-20m and partially pulled Accenture, Teleperformance and Concentrix. Hi-tech clients moved first because they can see AI use-cases in their own workflows and several now run in-house models. Non-tech enterprises are following on price: 20-30% discounts are being sought on new contracts, which is producing vendor consolidation and share loss to mid-tier names (Persistent, Mphasis, Coforge, Zensar all growing double digits while tier-1 does not). Three of the top five reported a sequential operating margin decline in Q1 FY27, Infosys the exception. Nifty IT is 13.0% of the index (INFY 5.5, TCS 4.0, HCLTECH 1.6, WIPRO 1.0, TECHM 0.9).
factors.transmission: This is a REVENUE-BASE factor, not a demand-cycle one, and that is what makes it different from every other headwind in this library. A demand slowdown postpones spend; AI deflation shrinks the price of the same delivered work — HCLTech's CEO put it as 'a $100m deal is now an $80m deal'. It therefore does not mean-revert when budgets recover, and it compounds: BNP Paribas puts the drag at ~3pp of annual revenue growth for another three to five years, Ambit at 15-20% cumulative over three to four years (3-4%/yr) and says the industry is not yet halfway through the cycle. Margins take a second hit from the cost side, because wage bills are 50-60% of costs and have not shrunk while AI skilling and partnership spend add 1-2%. A third effect is on VISIBILITY rather than level: as pricing moves from headcount-based billing to business-outcome deals, revenue is harder to recognise early, which widens the distribution of quarterly prints and is a reason to expect larger results-day moves in the sector, not smaller. DISTINCT FROM ai_capex_roi: that factor is about the BUYERS of AI compute and reaches India through global beta; this one is about the SELLERS of IT services and reaches the index through 13% of its weight directly. Cheap tokens are the shared cause; the two legs transmit on different clocks.

facts.note: Google cut ~$50m from a ~$200m annual HCLTech contract covering part of its application development and engineering work — a cost-efficiency programme repurposing budget to AI, applied across several IT partners. Wipro's deal with Meta trimmed by $15-20m; Meta also partially pulled Accenture, Teleperformance and Concentrix.
facts.source: Moneycontrol; corroborated by StartupTalky, CIO Tech Outlook, Digital Terminal

facts.note: Clients seeking 20-30% discounts on new contracts across telecom, SaaS, hi-tech and financial services (Gaurav Vasu, UnearthInsight). Intense competition for the same accounts is driving vendor consolidation at lower price points. UnearthInsight expects sector operating margins down 0.5-1pp cumulatively in FY27.

Ambit (Ashwin Mehta) after Q1 FY27: deflation is running at the LOW end of what companies guided and 'could be higher going forward'; the industry has not passed the midway point of the cycle. BNP Paribas (Kumar Rakesh): at least 3pp of annual revenue growth lost to AI deflation for another 3-5 years.
facts.source: Moneycontrol; Ambit note of late June 2026 (15-20% cumulative over 3-4 years)

facts.note: HCLTech CEO C Vijayakumar quantified it on the Q4 FY26 call: 'Let's say something was a $100 million deal, now could be an $80 million deal' — estimated impact ~2-3% a year.

The repo's own screen agrees on the delivery side and disagrees on the price. Every IT constituent FAILS the delivered-growth leg on 5-year net profit CAGR (INFY 8.8%, TCS 8.7%, HCLTECH 8.3%, WIPRO 4.1%, TECHM 1.7% against a 10% bar) while three of five pass consistency at 88.9% — they grew almost every year, slowly. But implied forward growth is NOT uniformly low: INFY is priced for +3.9% and WIPRO +9.7%, whereas HCLTECH is priced for +24.6% on 3.9% delivered over three years and TECHM for +50.1% on -0.1%. The deflation is priced into the two cheapest names and not into the two carrying the largest expectation gaps — and HCLTech is the name that just lost a quarter of its Google contract.

watch: Deal TCV versus deal REVENUE. Renegotiations show up as flat-to-lower revenue on unchanged or rising TCV — a book-to-bill that looks fine while pricing erodes underneath.
Sequential operating margin, not YoY. Three of the top five fell QoQ in Q1 FY27; the sector-wide guide is -0.5 to -1pp cumulatively across FY27.

Mid-tier growth minus tier-1 growth (Persistent, Coforge, Mphasis, Zensar). A widening spread is vendor consolidation moving share DOWN-market, which is the share-loss channel rather than the demand channel.
Hi-tech client concentration in the disclosures — those accounts renegotiated first and are the leading indicator for the non-tech verticals.

Whether outcome-based pricing shows up as WIDER results-day moves. If revenue becomes harder to forecast, the sector's earnings-day distribution should fatten; earnings_reactions.json is where that would be visible.
The expectation gap, not the news. INFY at +3.9% implied has little left to disappoint; HCLTECH at +24.6% and TECHM at +50.1% are the names where a deflation print collides with a multiple.

factors.name: Domestic policy / regulatory risk
factors.status: RBI draft norms (7 Aug) restricting revolving-credit products at non-bank lenders remain uncleared — Bajaj Finance fell 4-5% (Rs 33k cr) on the day and is still -1.46% over the last three sessions. COUNTER-EVIDENCE arrived on 12 August: Bank of America agreed to acquire up to 49.9% of Jio Financial's Jio Credit for up to Rs 18,268 crore ($1.9bn). A global bank underwriting an Indian NBFC at that size, five days after the draft, argues against the most severe reading of it. The market has not yet made that connection.
factors.transmission: The POLICY channel is distinct from the macro channel: it hits specific business models directly (here: NBFC revolving credit), and because financials are ~35-38% of the index, a financials-specific policy shock moves Nifty without any macro deterioration. Keeping this separate from the oil/geopolitics factor makes regime classification cleaner — policy days are rotation days, not risk-off days.

factors.name: Earnings (Q1 FY27 season)
factors.status: Q1 FY27 prints are BEATING and being SOLD. Apollo Hospitals PAT +38.4% YoY to Rs 610 cr on revenue +20.6% — stock -3.49%. Grasim consolidated PAT +51% to Rs 2,146 cr on revenue +21% — stock -3.79%. Tata Motors CV PAT +83.3% to Rs 2,560 cr, but flattered by a one-time gain from Tata Capital — the only one of the three that rose. The pattern is the Expectation panel's arithmetic in action: trailing P/E over forward P/E already embeds a growth rate, so a genuine +38% can still miss what the multiple assumed. Underneath, mid-teens revenue growth with high-single-digit PAT persists; Emkay's FY27 Nifty EPS +14% needs margin relief that Brent at $88 does not supply.
factors.transmission: The medium-term driver everything else feeds into: sustained cheap oil → margin recovery → the +14% EPS hope becomes upgrades → the only durable path above 25k.

facts.note: Three Q1 FY27 beats (Apollo +38% PAT, Grasim +51%, Tata Motors +83%) — two of the three stocks fell
Q1 FY27: revenue growth mid-teens, PAT growth high-single-digit; margin compression the key theme
Bright spots: Bajaj Finance +28%, M&M, industrials; IT muted

factors.name: GST cuts & consumption
factors.status: Sept-2025 GST cuts still feeding through; one GDP print at 8.2%; autos/durables strongest. The quiet structural positive under the noise.
factors.transmission: Domestic demand floor under cyclicals (autos, durables, retail, cement) — supports the DII bid narrative even when FIIs sell.

facts.note: GST reforms boosting consumption; growth outlook revised up; an 8.2% quarterly GDP print
